closeout.summary: Named order-line holds, fail-closed reserve, cancel-to-history release, and one-way full-hold pack at Packed. Pack Some, Pack All, and Unpack wait.

current_focus.summary: Build platform-neutral stock.pack: Processing to Packed consumes one named hold in full. On-hand and reserved both drop. Packed is one-way. Pack Some, Pack All, and Unpack wait. Unpaid 60-minute cancel stays Commerce calling existing stock.release. No GUI, CLI, Worker auth, live Commerce, Woo, Katana, deploy, or PR 20 mix.

decisions.question: What is the next Inventory-owned kernel slice after the transfer-list read model?
decisions.rationale: The reserved balance field already exists and is preserved by opening, adjust, and transfer, but nothing writes a reservation record. Commerce cannot sell without reserve/release. CHARTER already names reservation records and order references as Inventory-owned. Stock-in and site mapping do not unblock selling.

decisions.choice: A named hold. Inventory mints a permanent opaque reservation ID. The record names one explicit pool, one active location, one managed SKU, one exact positive quantity, and one public-safe order/line reference. No customer, address, or payment data. This cycle creates the hold and cancels it. Packing, expiry, and whole-cart documents wait.

decisions.question: What is one reservation?
decisions.rationale: CHARTER already requires Inventory-owned reservation records and order references so a later admin view can show order number, quantity, and location. A naked reserved counter cannot do that. One SKU-location line keeps the first commands inspectable; a cart is several holds, not one blob. Packing is a different command that consumes a hold.

decisions.choice: No. Reserve fails closed when available is less than the requested quantity. No reservation record, no reserved bump, durable business rejection. Available is on-hand minus existing order reservations minus outgoing transfer commitments. Transfers may warn and go negative; sales may not. No backorder flag in this slice.

decisions.question: If available stock is not enough, does reserve still create a hold?
decisions.rationale: Reservations are the customer-order quantity that already has priority over transfers. Allowing a sale hold to go negative would reintroduce oversell. Backorder is a later explicit command flag, not a silent default and not a read of Commerce settings.

decisions.choice: One active hold per pool and order/line reference. A new reserve whose location, SKU, and quantity match returns the original hold. Different contents under that same order/line conflict. Exact command-ID retry still returns the original terminal result. This does not replace quantity; replacement is a later edit or release-then-reserve.

decisions.question: If checkout asks twice for the same order line, what happens?
decisions.rationale: A second hold for the same order line would double-count reserved stock and oversell. This matches sku.register: same identity returns the original, changed contents conflict. Command-ID replay remains the CHARTER timeout rule and is not a second business key.

decisions.choice: Cancel is an awaited command, not a hard delete. The hold stays as durable canceled history, reserved stock returns to available, and one immutable receipt records the actor and effects. The same order/line may reserve again after cancel, which mints a new reservation ID. Exact command-ID retry returns the original cancel result. Already-canceled or missing holds reject. Packing still waits.

decisions.question: When a hold is canceled, what remains?
decisions.rationale: CHARTER forbids rewriting history. Canceled transfers already keep Done/Canceled records and release planning stock. A deleted hold would leave only a receipt and could not answer which order released which quantity. Uniqueness applies to active holds, so a later checkout for the same order line is a new hold, not a resurrection of the canceled ID.

decisions.choice: Consume happens at Packed. Processing → Packed takes reserved stock off the shelf: on-hand and reserved both drop, and the hold becomes packed history. Payment confirmation only moves the order from Hold to Processing and does not change counts. Shipped/label/Delivered after Packed does not change counts again. Partial pack waits.

history.choice: The Inventory hold stays reserved from checkout through Processing. Payment confirmation does not change counts. Consume happens when a shipping label is applied (Shipped): on-hand and reserved both drop, and the hold becomes packed/consumed history. Packed is not a separate Inventory status this cycle. Processing is wait-to-pack only.

decisions.question: Which order step takes reserved stock off the shelf?
decisions.rationale: Bobby: Processing → Packed is when inventory leaves reserved and actually reduces. Matches Katana Packed (in stock and committed both drop; Delivered after Packed is no further movement). Woo/Shopify unpaid timeout is a different command (release/cancel), not consume.

decisions.choice: Unpaid Hold/Pending Payment never becomes Processing. After 60 minutes it is Cancelled and Inventory release returns reserved stock to available. Processing → Packed is unrelated. The unpaid clock is an order/Commerce timer that calls existing stock.release; this packing slice does not add an Inventory cron. 60 minutes matches WooCommerce Hold stock (minutes) default. Shopify has no matching unpaid-order auto-cancel; checkout only holds stock for a few minutes during payment.

decisions.question: If payment never arrives, what happens to the hold, and after how long?
decisions.rationale: Bobby asked to cancel unpaid holds instead of sending them to Processing, and to check Shopify/Woo for the length. WooCommerce Products → Inventory Hold stock default is 60 minutes, then unpaid pending orders cancel and restock. Shopify does not expose a 60-minute unpaid-order setting. Smoky ordering is Woo-first, so 60 minutes is the shop-familiar default. Inventory already has cancel-to-history release.

decisions.choice: One awaited command names one active reservation ID and consumes the full remaining quantity. On-hand and reserved both drop by that amount. Exact command-ID retry returns the original packed result. Missing, already-packed, or canceled holds reject. Pack Some (partial quantity) and Pack All (every hold on the order) are named later growth, not this slice.

decisions.question: What does one pack command consume?
decisions.rationale: Bobby: A to start, with Pack Some and Pack All listed as what we want to grow into. This cycle is one hold, full quantity, like transfer receive. Partial and whole-cart packing stay explicit later work, not silent flags.

decisions.choice: Packed is one-way this cycle. Unpack/revert is deferred and named for later implementation. A mistake is not silently rewritten.

history.choice: Not this cycle. Packed is terminal for that hold. Unpack/revert waits, same as Received reversion on transfers. A mistake is a new hold plus a reasoned adjustment, or a later unpack command.

decisions.question: If they packed the wrong bag, can they undo it?
decisions.rationale: Bobby: Packed with unpack deferred and noted for later. Matches transfer Received: first slice is one-way so the kernel is inspectable.

recommendation.reason: Reserve and release exist. Selling still cannot take a held bag off the shelf. Packing is the next Inventory-owned writer. Expiry and Commerce transport do not consume physical stock.
recommendation.recommended: packing/commit: consume a named hold into physical stock when an order is packed
